definitions: To have a direct effect or influence on a situation or person.
examples: The new company policies will impact how employees manage their daily work schedules.

definitions: One of several things that cause or influence something that happens.
examples: Cost is a major factor when choosing which university you want to attend.
Price is an important factor when buying a car.
Stress is a major factor in illness.

definitions: A particular way of thinking about or dealing with something.
examples: We need to try a different approach because the first plan failed completely.

definitions: An abstract idea or general principle about how something works.
examples: Although the concept was difficult, the teacher explained it very clearly.
The teacher explained the basic concepts of physics.
Their business concept proved successful.

definitions: A particular way of considering or judging a situation.
examples: Traveling abroad gave her a broader perspective on different world cultures.
He has a very different perspective on the problem.

definitions: A fact or event that is observed to exist or happen.
examples: Social media networking has become a global phenomenon over the last decade.

definitions: The quality of being important or having a noticeable meaning.
examples: Scientists have understood the true significance of this discovery only recently.

definitions: A belief that something is true even without proof.
examples: His assumption was wrong because he had not checked the official data.
Her argument rests on several questionable assumptions.

definitions: A series of actions that you take to achieve a result.
examples: Learning a foreign language is a slow process that requires daily practice.

definitions: A planned and systematic way of doing a particular activity.
examples: They tested a new teaching method to help students improve their reading.

definitions: Something that is considered more important than other things.
examples: Safety must remain our highest priority while working on the construction site.

definitions: A personal opinion or way of looking at a situation.
examples: Although I respect your viewpoint, I still disagree with your final conclusion.

definitions: A necessary or essential part of a larger whole.
examples: Trust is a fundamental element in building strong and lasting personal relationships.
Trust is a key element in friendship.
Water and air are basic elements.

definitions: A particular feature or part of a problem or subject.
examples: We should consider every aspect of the project before making a final decision.
Safety is an important aspect of driving.
Consider every aspect of the problem.

definitions: A set of official steps for doing something correctly.
examples: All passengers must follow the standard security procedure at the airport.

definitions: A special skill or way of doing an activity efficiently.
examples: She practiced a quiet breathing technique to calm her nerves before speaking.

definitions: The quality of being important or having a large effect.
examples: Parents often emphasize the importance of getting a good education early in life.
She stressed the importance of regular study.
The topic is of global importance.

definitions: The degree to which something is connected or applicable to a topic.
examples: The professor questioned the relevance of those statistics to our current topic.

definitions: The details or history that explain a situation or person.
examples: Her technical background helped her solve the software issue very quickly.
She has a background in music.
They come from different backgrounds.

definitions: A subject that is discussed, written about, or studied.
examples: Climate change has become a frequent topic during international news broadcasts.

definitions: A particular way in which something repeatedly happens or develops.
examples: Researchers noticed a clear pattern in consumer buying habits during holidays.

definitions: An inclination to act or behave in a particular way.
examples: He has a tendency to arrive late when meetings start early morning.

definitions: The chance or probability that a particular event will happen.
examples: There is a high likelihood of rain, so bring an umbrella today.

definitions: A required or agreed level of quality and achievement.
examples: The hotel maintains a high standard of service for all its guests.

definitions: Something impressive that has been successfully completed through effort.
examples: Graduating from university was a proud accomplishment for the entire family.

definitions: Physical or mental energy needed to achieve a particular result.
examples: Although the project required much effort, the final result was outstanding.
It took a lot of effort to climb the hill.
She put great effort into her homework.

definitions: An act of trying to do something, especially something difficult.
examples: She made a brave attempt to climb the steep mountain trail yesterday.
She passed the exam on her second attempt.
His first attempt at baking was successful.

definitions: Movement toward an improved state, goal, or higher development level.
examples: The student has made great progress in speaking English since joining class.

definitions: The process of making something better, or a positive change.
examples: There has been a noticeable improvement in air quality across the city.
Her grades showed dramatic improvement.
Make minor improvements to the report.

definitions: A situation or object that prevents movement or blocks progress.
examples: Lack of funding proved to be a major obstacle for the team.

definitions: A rule, structure, or problem that prevents people from advancing.
examples: High costs can create a financial barrier for students seeking higher education.
Language can be a barrier to communication.
Safety barriers lined the racetrack.

definitions: An official rule that limits or controls what people can do.
examples: The city council placed a travel restriction during the severe winter storm.

definitions: Something that is necessary or mandatory according to official rules.
examples: A valid passport is a necessary requirement for traveling to foreign countries.

definitions: A typical or important quality, part, or characteristic of something.
examples: The main feature of this new smartphone is its long battery life.
The smartphone has many new camera features.
Read the special feature in the magazine.

definitions: A quality or trait that typically belongs to a person or thing.
examples: Patience is a key characteristic of an effective and successful teacher.
Kindness is her best characteristic.
List the physical characteristics of mammals.

definitions: Extremely important or necessary for the success or failure of something.
examples: Water is crucial for the survival of all living organisms.
Timing proved crucial to the success of the plan.

definitions: Forming a necessary base or core; of central importance.
examples: Freedom of speech is a fundamental human right.
Trust is fundamental to any successful partnership.

definitions: Having no purpose or sense; serving no useful function.
examples: It is pointless to argue about something that cannot be changed.

definitions: Latent qualities or abilities that may be developed and lead to future success.
examples: The young athlete shows great potential for the upcoming Olympics.

definitions: Having or showing the capacity to develop into something in the future.
examples: We need to identify potential risks before launching the project.
We have many potential customers.

definitions: The state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or be imagined.
examples: She had to face the harsh reality of the economic situation.
The reality of the situation is quite difficult.

definitions: Not showing or considering things as they are in reality; impractical.
examples: Expecting to learn a new language fluently in a week is unrealistic.

definitions: Absolutely necessary or essential for life or success.
examples: Clear communication plays a vital role in team productivity.

definitions: correct, precise, and free from errors in detail
examples: Providing accurate contact details is essential on your visa application.
The weather forecast was remarkably accurate.
Provide accurate measurements for the table.

definitions: clearly stated, decided, or established beyond doubt
examples: We have a definite moving date set for the middle of next month.

definitions: having the necessary requirements or meeting conditions to do something
examples: Permanent residents are eligible to apply for state health benefits after six months.
Only permanent employees are eligible for the bonus.

definitions: a strong belief that something will happen or be the case in the future
examples: Managing your realistic expectations helps prevent disappointment during a international move.
The event exceeded all our expectations.
High expectations can create pressure.

definitions: arrangements or intentions made for upcoming periods of time
examples: Discussing future plans with your family helps set clear relocation goals.

definitions: an act or duty to which a person is morally or legally bound
examples: Tenants have a legal obligation to pay monthly rent on the agreed date.

definitions: a punishment or financial fine imposed for breaking a rule, law, or contract clause
examples: Terminating a tenancy contract prematurely incurs a financial cancellation penalty.

definitions: activities that improve awareness, talent, potential, and employability skills
examples: Living in a foreign country offers unmatched opportunities for lifelong personal development.

definitions: marked by exactness and accuracy of detail or performance
examples: Provide precise measurements when ordering custom furniture for your new flat.

definitions: duties or tasks that an individual is accountable for performing
examples: Accepting a managerial position brings increased workplace responsibilities.

definitions: the act of presenting a document or application for consideration or judgment
examples: After online document submission, you will receive an official confirmation reference number.

definitions: showing a great deal of variety; very different from one another
examples: The international school boasts a culturally diverse student body representing forty countries.
The company prides itself on its diverse workforce.

definitions: serving to describe or depict something clearly using detailed language
examples: The travel guide includes vivid descriptive passages detailing historical architecture in the city center.

definitions: using or spending resources, money, or time carelessly, inefficiently, or extravagantly
examples: Leaving heating running in unoccupied rooms is environmentally wasteful and increases utility bills.

definitions: A significant moment of progress, discovery, or clarity.
examples: Having her first fluent conversation in Spanish was a breakthrough moment.

definitions: A state of emotional and mental tranquility and harmony.
examples: Attending the mountain retreat helped her rediscover inner peace.

definitions: To expose oneself or something valuable to danger, harm, or loss.
examples: You shouldn't risk your health by working without taking breaks.

definitions: To include someone or something as an important or prominent aspect.
examples: The new mobile application will feature automated voice translation.

definitions: To be important or to have an effect on a situation.
examples: It does not matter if you arrive a little late.

definitions: To face a problem means to deal with it.
examples: We must face the facts.
She faced a difficult choice.

definitions: A look is the way someone or something appears.
examples: She has a new look.
I like the look of this room.

definitions: To raise something means to increase it.
examples: The shop raised its prices.
We need to raise the temperature.

definitions: The rest is the part that is left.
examples: I ate some cake and gave the rest to my sister.
The rest of the class was quiet.

definitions: Room is empty space that is available for something.
examples: There is room for one more person in the car.
Make room for the cake.

definitions: To store something means to keep it for later use.
examples: We store the boxes in the garage.
Store the files on your computer.

definitions: Support is help or encouragement that you give to someone.
examples: Thank you for your support.
The team needs more support from fans.

definitions: Wear is damage caused by using something for a long time.
examples: The carpet shows signs of wear.
Check the tyres for wear.

definitions: If something holds a number of things, it has space for them.
examples: The hall holds two hundred people.
This bottle holds one litre.

definitions: The order of things is the way they are arranged one after another.
examples: Put the pictures in the correct order.
The names are in alphabetical order.

definitions: A run is a series of similar events.
examples: The team had a run of bad luck.
The show had a long run in London.

definitions: A set price or plan is fixed and does not change.
examples: The menu is a set price.
We follow a set routine every morning.

definitions: A form of something is a type or kind of it.
examples: Cycling is a healthy form of exercise.
What form of transport do you use?

definitions: To support something means to hold it up.
examples: The columns support the roof.
A strong frame supports the mattress.

definitions: A support is a thing that holds something up.
examples: The bridge needs a strong support.
The roof rests on wooden supports.

definitions: If a job or place is open, it is available for someone to take or use.
examples: The position is still open.
The scholarship is open to all students.

definitions: Someone who is free is not busy and can do something.
examples: Are you free this evening?
The doctor is free now.

definitions: A key thing is very important.
examples: Trust is key to a good friendship.
She played a key role in the project.

definitions: A stage is a period or phase in a process.
examples: The project is at an early stage.
Children go through several stages of development.
